body:
Installed forge-bestofboth v3 (the "fail-bounded, not foolproof" charter) as a new skill and ran two passes against SLS(92)/10.06 per its own Phase-0 sequencing (safety spine before anything else).

WARRANT#109 -> SLS(93)/10.07: audited OptimizePrecisionLotSize end to end. Found baseRiskPercent is properly clamped to MaxRiskPercent (7.5% default), but a SEPARATE downstream multiplier stack (_comb, bounded 0.50-2.50, folding in regime/conviction/memory/predictive/validation/awareness confidence signals) multiplies riskAmount again -- neither stack knows about the other. Worst-case realized risk-at-stop under default settings was up to 18.75% of account base (7.5% x 2.5), silently exceeding what the code's own comments document as its 7.5% ceiling. This reproduces under normal legitimate operation whenever every confidence signal peaks at once -- not a misconfiguration. Added HARD_MAX_RISK_PERCENT_PER_TRADE, a #define (not an input) reusing the same 7.5 value already documented as the ceiling -- no input, gated flag, ratchet, or message can raise it. Reduce-only, fires only in the rare simultaneous-max tail case.

WARRANT#110 -> SLS(94)/10.08: added a session-scoped counter for how often the new hard floor actually fires, reported in the shutdown summary alongside existing session stats. 0 is a real, expected answer, not evidence the mechanism is dead.

Both compiled 0 errors (1 pre-existing unrelated sesMap warning). Diff-verified purely additive at each step. Neither live-tested yet -- deployed to the terminal's real Experts folder, forge_ledger.json updated in both locations (now pass_91). Not yet attempted: the charter's other two Phase-0 items (the full logging/change-ledger spine, and a fresh boundary audit against the 11-class taxonomy) -- flagged as the next items under this charter, not squeezed into this two-pass session.
